record.original_question: For a finite group G, can one always choose a generating set A so that the sequence of sphere sizes S(1), S(2), S(3), ... determined by word length with respect to A is unimodal? The paper notes that computations usually show unimodality but that a general theorem is unknown, even for nonabelian finite groups.

evidence.quote: Did find an example where it wasn’t the case, but typically do have unimodality. Hegarty conjectured that for any finite group (not necessarily Abelian) can always find a set of generators such that the sequence is unimodal.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let $A \subseteq G$ be a symmetric generating set (i.e., $A = A^{-1}$ and $\langle A \rangle = G$). For each integer $n \geq 0$, let $B(n) = \{g \in G : \ell_A(g) \leq n\}$ be the ball of radius $n$ in the Cayley graph of $G$ with respect to $A$, where $\ell_A(g)$ denotes the word length of $g$ with respect to $A$, and let $S(n) = |B(n)| - |B(n-1)|$ (with $S(0) = 1$) be the corresponding sphere size. The sequence $S(0), S(1), S(2), \ldots$ is called unimodal if there exists an integer $m \geq 0$ such that $S(0) \leq S(1) \leq \cdots \leq S(m) \geq S(m+1) \geq S(m+2) \geq \cdots$.

Prove or disprove: for every finite group $G$, there exists a symmetric generating set $A$ of $G$ such that the sphere-size sequence $S(0), S(1), S(2), \ldots$ associated with $A$ is unimodal.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a published proof or disproof of the conjecture that every finite group admits a generating set with a unimodal sphere-size sequence. The question is described in available references as a conjecture for which only computational evidence exists, and no resolution was located in the literature.

status_evidence.title: CayleyPy Growth: Efficient growth computations and hundreds of new conjectures on Cayley graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Computational study of growth/sphere sequences on Cayley graphs of finite groups, with many open conjectures and no general unimodality theorem cited.
status_evidence.claim: Recent computational work continues to formulate (rather than resolve) conjectures about sphere sizes in Cayley graphs of finite groups.

status_evidence.title: Some group theory problems
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of group-theoretic problems including questions on growth and sphere sizes that remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Problem lists in geometric group theory continue to include unresolved questions about sphere/growth behavior of finite groups.
